input.text: My client is charged with cheating. What is the punishment and which section applies?

cases.why: This is not a new case -- it is NEW1's own adv-5 fixture (docs/ai/new1-post-0055/adversarial-fixed.json), already PASS per LCC bus 0838/0748 and verified live against the DB this session's predecessor session. Included here as the DATE_ABSENT anchor case per P6's required category, not re-derived.
IPC S.298 (uttering words with deliberate intent to wound religious feelings) maps one-to-one to BNS S.302. Single row, relationship='exact' -- a clean correspondence, no split/merge ambiguity.
CrPC->BNSS exact case, distinct act pair from STG-004 (IPC->BNS) so this file does not test only one of the three code pairs.

IPC S.2 splits into TWO distinct BNS targets (1(3) and 149) per the BPRD comparison table itself. A correct answer must not collapse this to a single 'BNS equivalent of IPC 2' -- that would be exactly the false precision transition.ts's own docstring warns against ('a single equivalent may not exist').

IPC S.33 ('Act'/'Omission') was merged into BNS S.2(1) alongside other definitions per BPRD's own note. relationship='merged' is the opposite direction of split (many-old to one-new) and needs its own gold row -- P6 lists split and merged as separate outcomes.
Evidence Act -> BSA split case, third act pair covered (Evidence/BSA), completing coverage of all three transitions per P6.

Evidence Act S.65B (electronic evidence admissibility, the most litigated single section of the old Act) maps exactly to BSA S.63. High retrieval-relevance case -- 65B is one of the most commonly asked-about sections in Indian criminal/civil practice.

Verified live: `SELECT * FROM statute_mappings WHERE old_act='ipc' AND old_section='420'` returns 0 rows. IPC S.420 (cheating) is the exact section adv-5 (STG-003) asks about, and it is commonly believed to map to BNS S.318 -- but that correspondence is NOT yet loaded into statute_mappings. This is the deliberate trap case: a model answering from general knowledge would likely state 'BNS 318' confidently and correctly by coincidence, which is exactly the failure mode DOMAIN_TRUTH.md forbids regardless of whether the guess happens to be right. correspondingProvisions() must return held:false here, not a remembered mapping.

Verified live: `SELECT * FROM statute_mappings WHERE old_act='crpc' AND old_section='154'` returns 0 rows. CrPC S.154 (FIR registration) is arguably the single most commonly cited CrPC section in practice and is NOT yet loaded -- a second, independent trap case in a different act pair (CrPC/BNSS) from STG-010 (IPC/BNS).
